steps.text: Beat butter and sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in egg until well combined, then stir in vanilla. Combine flour and salt in a separate bowl; add to butter mixture and mix to form a dough. Cover dough with plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Chill 2 cookie sheets in the refrigerator.
Transfer chilled dough to a cookie press; press out onto the chilled cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are lightly golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer cookies to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This simple butter cookie recipe can be made as a drop cookie, used in a cookie press, or shaped into a roll and sliced. Perfect for baking with kids!

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make a simple but versatile butter cookie. It’s a great recipe for making pressed cookies, drop cookies, or rolled-and-sliced round cookies. And no matter how you make them, they're terrific decorated Christmas cookies.

review.reviewBody: Great, simple spritz butter cookies! Not too sweet, but nice and buttery. This recipe made 4 trays full, about 5 dozen cookies not including the gobs of dough my 4 year old swiped. One hint - you probably won't need to refrigerate the dough to use in a cookie press unless it's really hot in your kitchen. We used dough at room temp and the cookies came out perfect on our first try. This one's a keeper!

I've been using this recipe for YEARS! I add orange zest & chopped dried cranberries, roll into logs, wrap in waxed paper, and chill. When chilled, I then brush the logs with beaten egg, then roll in raw/turbinado sugar, slice, then bake according to the recipe. End result is a tender buttery cookie with the tang of cranberries, the perfume of orange, and a raw sugar rim that gives the edges an almost gemlike appearance. This has been a favorite request (along with my chocolate/cayenne/orange shortbread!) - I can't recommend this recipe, enough! ❤️

This is one of the best spritz/butter cookie recipes I've used. However, I did make some slight changes. I reduced my flour by a 1/4 cup, I added a 1/4 cup more butter and also used almond extract with the vanilla. Also, I found that 400 degrees F was to high even for just 8 minutes but 375 degrees F was perfect at 8 minutes....nice color and texture! I've saved this recipe and will share.

I'm an '80s baby. When I was in kindergarten, 36 years ago, in Memphis, we had the BEST butter cookies at school. This recipe, minus the egg, comes REALLY close. If you want the butter cookies that crumble in your hands as you eat them, leave out the egg. If you want a chewy cookie, add the egg. Other that that, GREAT RECIPE!!

Okay, I just made them the 3rd time. I’m trying to quit smoking and those cookies are a prize I make for myself on Friday as I survived another week without nicotine. They are sweet, they are buttery, they take like 5 minutes to mix, they can be mixed with a regular spatula… I don’t pipe them, instead I freeze the batter rolled into plastic wrap and stuck into empty paper towel roll. It takes 20 minutes of freezing and than they can be cut into cookies. With these small modifications this is honestly the laziest recipe ever. It requires similar amount of effort to making pasta with jarred sauce. Best cookies ever!!!

Loved this simple recipe that doesn't use baking soda or powder. The only 4 small changes I made were:
1. Lowered flour to 2 1/4 cups.
2. Rolled dough with hands into 3 logs wrapped in sealing wrap, so I could use at different times.
3. Rolled balls in cin/sugar mixture before baking.
4. Baked them at 375.
Important...have butter soft at room temperature before creaming.

I added 1 teaspoon of baking powder in thinking it won't rise without baking powder. My cookies tasted buttery and not So sweet...delicious!..crispy and buttery..I also wanted to be creative --- I wanted to make jelly filled cookies, but thought their recipes would yield flavorless cookies(and that the only thing good would be the jam). I tried putting a dollop of jam in the center of these cookies to make "buttery jelly filled cookies." I just pressed down in the center of the cookie making a penny sized well or so, and scooped on jam...I baked them at 350 first to see I'd they would cook, but seems like for my oven, they needed to be at 400. So I raised the temperature to 400 and baked until edges are golden brown...which should take around 10 minutes or So. The cookies don't have to be brown in color..They probably taste best at a beige color with ONLY golden EDGES. My cookies stayed white, revealing the color of the jam in the middle..soo pretty. Thank you soo much for the recipe. Those who gave this recipe 1's are people that didn't follow instructions and don't know how to bake.

I love these cookies. I cut the flour to 2 1/2 cups and make drop cookies (no need to chill). The last batch I made, I left out the vanilla and added 1 teaspoon of lemon juice and 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest. They're wonderful! Very delicate lemon flavor.

This is a great recipe you can do lots with. I've baked for over 50 yrs so I'm not afraid to try different things. I doubled the recipe and added an 8oz block of cream cheese and beat it up with the butter and sugar because we like soft cookies. The cookies came out fantastic, soft, and held up great in the oven. Because of Christmas I put sprinkles on top before baking, but you can do a lot with these. Don't be afraid to get creative. Just remember to keep the dough cold. While baking some I kept the rest in the fridge until I was ready for it.

I mixed the dough and refrigerated for about 2 hrs. When I tried to put it in my cookie press, it was much too stiff. I used it for rolled cookies, using the smooth side of a plastic cutting board. I used about a baseball siize piece of dough at a time. The dough rolled out to the 1/4 inch so easy. I did not use any additional flour to the well chilled dough. I made large snowflake cut outs, about 4 inches in diameter. Chill the cookie sheets. A double batch made 30 of these large cookies. Baked in a convection over at 375 for 10 to 12 minutes. They taste absolutely wonderful. And so easy to roll. I will frost tomorrow . Thanks for this amazing recipe.

This recipe is great! Since I don't have a lunch period at school, I make these. People ask me for these cookies, and they think that I bought them because of how tasty they are! I didn't chill the dough, and it came out great. Also, I added one extra egg. A must-make.
My kids love it so much! They keep asking me to bake again! Thanks for the recipe.

I’ve made these cookies a few times now and they are fool proof! Even without chilling the dough or the cookie sheets the cookies came out great. Instead of a mixer I used the dough blade in my food processor. One time I added mini marshmallows which melted and caramelized which was also delicious. I baked on parchment each time.

Made twice. No cookie press so I just got some plastic wrap and rolled the dough. Cut into thin slices and baked at 400f for 10 minutes. Made as written the first time. Added ground cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves just for fun and turned out good! As written and add-ins are both good for this recipe! Big hit with the family. I think dipping them in some melted chocolate next time will be a hit
I made squares with sesame seeds
One of the easiest, flavorful cookie recipes my family and friends 🧡
Its simple and delicious! So easy to make.
Wouldn't go thru cookie press. Rock hard.
Simple to follow. Glad to find a recipe that uses a cookie press. Better recipe than found in book that came with press.
Wow these are delicious 😋
